name: How do tub-to-shower conversions affect home resale value in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Will removing a bathtub and adding a shower help or hurt resale value in Los Angeles and nearby neighborhoods?
mainEntity.text: Will removing a bathtub and adding a shower help or hurt resale value in Los Angeles and nearby neighborhoods?

acceptedAnswer.text: The resale effect depends on how the home is used and who is likely to buy it. In many cases, a well-designed shower conversion adds appeal because buyers like modern finishes and easy access. That is especially true when the original tub is outdated, unused, or awkward. However, removing the only bathtub can reduce flexibility for families, which may matter in some markets. The quality of the remodel matters just as much as the fixture choice. A shower that looks custom, functions well, and matches the rest of the home is more likely to support value than a budget conversion that feels temporary. In Los Angeles-area neighborhoods, buyers often respond well to thoughtful bathroom updates, but they also notice workmanship. Homeowners should consider the number of baths in the home, whether another tub remains, and how the finished shower fits the property’s overall level. Resale value is strongest when the remodel improves both style and everyday function.
acceptedAnswer.description: It can help if the shower improves function, style, and accessibility, but it can hurt if the home loses its only bathtub or the finish quality looks out of place. The impact depends on the number of bathrooms and the likely buyer profile.
